description: Fair comparison configuration for register feature analysis. Adds opportunity normalization, log2 transformation, and optional weighting as a new analysis layer on top of the existing raw-count pipeline. The original pipeline is untouched.

design_principles.normalization_rationale: Divide raw event count by the number of eligible sites (contexts where that feature could have differed). This gives a per-opportunity rate that is independent of corpus size and linguistic level granularity.
design_principles.log2_rationale: Apply log2 to the normalized rate (not raw counts) to compress Zipfian frequency distributions. log2 of a rate produces a value in bits; a difference of 1 bit = the feature occurs twice as often in one register. Must apply AFTER normalization, not before.
design_principles.weighting_rationale: After log2(normalized rate), cross-level gaps are already compressed. Weighting is an optional further emphasis step to surface fine-grained features (e.g., morphological) relative to coarse-level features (e.g., constituency). Avoid over-weighting.
design_principles.cross_newspaper_comparability: Eligible site counts scale with corpus size, so dividing by them inherently normalizes for corpus size differences across newspapers (1041 vs 1148 vs 1500 sentence pairs).

linguistic_levels.description: Ordered from finest (1) to coarsest (7). Level index is used for level-based weighting: weight = 1 / level_index^alpha.

levels.label: Morphological
levels.description: Sub-token inflectional and morphological properties (FEATS column, verb morphology)

levels.label: Lexical / Token
levels.description: Word-level insertions, deletions, surface form changes, POS changes, word order

levels.label: Dependency / Syntactic
levels.description: Dependency relation and head changes (per-token syntactic role)

levels.label: Constituency / Phrasal
levels.description: Phrase-level constituency operations and clause type changes

levels.label: Register / Typological
levels.description: Sentence-level headline typology and structural register markers

levels.label: Structural / TED
levels.description: Holistic tree edit distance measures (one value per sentence pair)

eligible_site_definitions.description: Named denominators used in opportunity normalization. All computed from corpus data per newspaper. Canonical side used as baseline throughout.

sentence_pairs.description: Total number of canonical–reduced sentence pairs

tokens_canonical.description: Total token count in canonical sentences (integer IDs only, excludes multi-word tokens)
tokens_canonical.source: CoNLL-U canonical file: count rows with numeric ID

function_word_tokens_canonical.description: Tokens with UPOS in {DET, ADP, AUX, PART, CCONJ, SCONJ, PRON} in canonical
function_word_tokens_canonical.source: CoNLL-U canonical file: filter by upos

content_word_tokens_canonical.description: Tokens with UPOS in {NOUN, VERB, ADJ, ADV, PROPN} in canonical
content_word_tokens_canonical.source: CoNLL-U canonical file: filter by upos

verb_tokens_canonical.description: Tokens with UPOS in {VERB, AUX} in canonical
verb_tokens_canonical.source: CoNLL-U canonical file: filter by upos

morph_feature_slots_canonical.description: Total number of annotated morphological feature instances across all canonical tokens (sum of FEATS slot counts; underscore/empty FEATS contributes 0)
morph_feature_slots_canonical.source: CoNLL-U canonical file: for each token, count pipe-separated FEATS entries

aligned_token_pairs.description: Total count of canonical–reduced aligned token pairs across all sentence pairs. Approximated as sum of min(len_canonical_sentence, len_reduced_sentence) over all pairs; exact count available from aligner output if stored.
aligned_token_pairs.source: Approximation from CoNLL-U token counts per sentence; or aligner output

punct_tokens_canonical.description: Tokens with UPOS == PUNCT in canonical
punct_tokens_canonical.source: CoNLL-U canonical file: filter by upos == PUNCT

constituency_nodes_canonical.description: Total count of all non-terminal nodes (excluding leaves) in canonical constituency parse trees
constituency_nodes_canonical.source: Constituency parse file: traverse each tree, count internal nodes

clause_nodes_canonical.description: Total count of S, SBAR, SINV, SQ nodes in canonical constituency parse trees
clause_nodes_canonical.source: Constituency parse file: traverse each tree, count S/SBAR/SINV/SQ nodes

feature_taxonomy.description: Per-feature level assignment and eligible site denominator. Features in excluded_features are omitted.

FEAT-CHG.notes: Each event = one (token, morph-attribute) pair differs between registers. Fine-grained per-value normalization: eligible sites for e.g. Tense changes = tokens with Tense annotation in canonical.

VERB-FORM-CHG.notes: Verb morphological form changes (VerbForm, Tense etc. on verbal tokens)

FW-DEL.notes: Function word deleted from canonical form

FW-ADD.notes: Function word added in reduced form (canonical lacks it). Using canonical FW count as baseline for consistency.

C-ADD.notes: Using canonical content word count as baseline

PUNCT-ADD.notes: Using canonical punct count as baseline

DEP-REL-CHG.notes: Each aligned token pair has exactly one dependency relation that could differ

CONST-MOV.notes: Each constituency node in canonical is a potential movement candidate

CONST-ADD.notes: Using canonical node count as baseline

CLAUSE-TYPE-CHG.notes: Denominator = clause nodes (S/SBAR/SINV/SQ) only, not all nodes

H-TYPE.notes: One headline type label per sentence pair

H-STRUCT.notes: One structural label per sentence pair

TED-SIMPLE.notes: TED score per sentence pair; canonical_value IS the numeric score. For score-based features, normalize by sentence_pairs to get mean score. Log2 applied to mean score. Do NOT use raw event count for TED.

excluded_features.description: Numeric/aggregate features that measure magnitude of change, not presence/absence of an event category. Excluded from normalization and weighting.

stage_1_raw.label: Raw counts
stage_1_raw.description: Original event counts from events_global.csv. Existing pipeline output, unchanged.

stage_2_opportunity_normalization.label: Opportunity-normalized rate
stage_2_opportunity_normalization.description: Divide raw count by eligible site count for the feature's level. Result is a per-opportunity rate in [0, 1] (approximately). For score-based features (TED), divide sum of scores by sentence_pairs to get mean score.
stage_2_opportunity_normalization.zero_handling: If count_raw == 0, rate_norm = 0.0 (genuine absence of the feature)

stage_3_log2.label: Log₂ of normalized rate
stage_3_log2.description: Apply log2 to the normalized rate. Compresses Zipfian distribution. A difference of 1 bit = feature occurs twice as often. Applied to rate_norm, not count_raw.
stage_3_log2.formula: log2_norm = log2(rate_norm + epsilon) where epsilon = 1e-9 to avoid log(0)
stage_3_log2.note: Values will be negative (since rate_norm < 1 in all practical cases); differences between features remain interpretable as bit differences.

stage_4_weighting.label: Weighted score (optional)
stage_4_weighting.description: Apply a weight to log2_norm. Each method is computed independently. Results are additive columns — all methods run and output simultaneously for comparison.

level.label: Level-based weight
level.description: Penalizes higher-level (coarser) features. Morphological features (level 1) get weight 1.0; constituency features (level 5) get weight 1/5^alpha.
level.alpha_note: alpha=1 is linear; alpha=0.5 is gentler. Configurable. Default 1.0.
level.applies_to: feature level (same weight for all values of a feature)

idf.label: IDF-analog weight
idf.description: Borrows TF-IDF intuition: features that are very frequent across the corpus get lower weight. Computed from the opportunity-normalized rates across all features.
idf.preferred_formula: log(1 / rate_norm) = -log(rate_norm) i.e. the negative log probability

jsd.label: Jensen-Shannon Divergence weight
jsd.description: Measures how much the feature's value distribution shifts between canonical and reduced registers. High JSD = feature is highly register-discriminating = upweighted. Requires value distribution per feature per register.
jsd.formula: weight_jsd = JSD(P_canonical(f) || P_reduced(f)) where P(f) is the distribution over feature values
jsd.note: JSD is in [0, log2(2)] = [0, 1] when using log2. Entirely data-driven.

pmi.label: PMI-based discriminativity weight
pmi.description: For each (feature, value) pair, computes Pointwise Mutual Information with the register label. High PMI = pair is register-specific. Aggregated to feature level by summing over values.
pmi.formula: pmi(f,v) = log2( P(v|register=canonical) / P(v) ); weight_pmi = sum_v max(0, pmi(f,v))
pmi.applies_to: feature-value pair level; aggregated to feature for summary

combined_score.description: Optional: combine normalization + weighting into a single score for ranking. Not applied by default — separate scores are more interpretable for publication.
combined_score.formula: score_combined = log2_norm * (weight_lvl * w1 + weight_idf * w2 + weight_jsd * w3) / (w1 + w2 + w3)
combined_score.note: Recommended to first compare methods separately (ablation) before combining.

task1.name: Comparative Register Study
new_visualizations: Opportunity-normalized feature frequency (bar chart, all features comparable)
Log2-normalized feature frequency (replaces raw count figures)
Level-weighted feature ranking (shows morphological features fairly)
Cross-newspaper comparison with normalized rates (fair across corpus sizes)
task1.note: Primary analysis layer. All four weighting methods computed and output for comparison.

task2.name: Transformation Study
new_visualizations: Normalized rule coverage by feature level
task2.note: Normalization applied to rule coverage rates. Weighting less central here since rules are already filtered by confidence. JSD/PMI weights carry over from Task 1 config.

task3.name: Complexity and Similarity Study
new_visualizations: Register profiles (log2-normalized feature vectors, one per register per newspaper)
Cross-level complexity contribution (normalized rates stacked by level)
Biber-style feature loading plot (PCA/factor analysis of normalized feature matrix)
task3.note: Log2-normalized rates serve as the feature vectors for complexity and similarity analyses. JSD weighting is most appropriate here since it directly measures register discriminativity.

implementation_modules.description: New Python modules to implement. All go under register_comparison/analysis/ (new subdirectory). Existing pipeline untouched.

key_methods: normalize(events_df, site_counts) -> DataFrame with rate_norm column
run(events_df, site_counts) -> DataFrame with both columns
apply_level_weights(df, alpha) -> DataFrame with score_lvl column
run_all(df) -> DataFrame with all weight columns

modules.purpose: Top-level runner. Loads config, runs pipeline for all 3 newspapers, saves CSVs and figures.
modules.cli: python run_fair_comparison.py [--newspapers ToI HT TH] [--methods level idf jsd pmi] [--no-plots]

output_columns_reference.eligible_site_count: Denominator used for normalization (numeric, per feature per newspaper)
output_columns_reference.eligible_site_name: Name of the eligible site (from eligible_site_definitions)
output_columns_reference.weight_jsd: JSD of value distribution between canonical and reduced registers
output_columns_reference.weight_pmi: Aggregated PMI of feature-value pairs with register label
